CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right ankle injury sustained during basketball.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Jerry is a 45-year-old male who presents with a right ankle injury sustained today while playing basketball with his son. Patient reports going up for a shot when his son collided with him while defending. Patient landed awkwardly and rolled/twisted his right ankle. He notes pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient reports difficulty walking and feels the ankle lacks stability. He recently returned to a regular workout routine at the gym and is concerned about interrupting his progress. Additionally, he volunteers as a basketball coach starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports lateral ankle pain with associated swelling and bruising. Denies medial ankle pain. Reports difficulty with ambulation due to pain and instability.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Patient recently returned to regular exercise and gym workouts.

MEDICATIONS
None reported prior to this visit.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Son Sean, age 10, plays basketball.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. Recently returned to regular gym workouts. Plays recreational basketball with his son. Volunteers as a basketball coach starting in April. Has dogs at home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented.
General: Alert, cooperative 45-year-old male.
Right ankle: Significant swelling on lateral side with bruising. Exquisite tenderness over lateral malleolus. Mild tenderness over medial deltoid region. Skin intact. Brisk capillary refill. No malalignment noted. Patient able to stand but unable to walk comfortably due to pain and instability.

RESULTS
Right ankle X-ray (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures. Fracture noted to be in an unstable position.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Displaced lateral malleolar fracture, right ankle (Weber C).

Plan:
1. Orthopedic surgery consultation for open reduction internal fixation with plate and screw fixation.
2. Non-weight bearing status with crutches provided.
3. Meloxicam prescribed for pain and swelling management.
4. Ice and elevation of ankle to reduce swelling. Patient works from home and can elevate regularly.
5. Expected recovery time approximately 3 months.
6. Patient counseled that he may need to sit out from his regular workout routine but can continue with coaching duties as tolerated.
7. Follow-up after surgery as arranged.
